question: A computer program that converts an entire program into machine language is called an:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Compiler**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **compiler **is a type of computer programme that turns an **entire programme into machine language** at once.
 
• A compiler is a programme that converts high-level code into object/machine code.
 
• A compiler is a **piece of software that converts code written** in one programming language (the source language) into code written in another programming language (the target language) (the target language).
 
• Compilers are a form of translator that helps digital devices, typically computers, communicate.
 
• Compilers are programmes that convert source code from a high-level programming language to a lower-level language (such as assembly language, object code, or machine code) in order to build an executable programme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **An interpreter's **job is to translate what someone says into a different language.
 
• **A simulator **is a programme or machine that creates a virtual version of a real-world situation, usually for the purposes of training or experimentation.
 
• **A computer device that converts **continuously varying analogue signals from instruments and sensors that monitor conditions such as sound, movement, and temperature into binary code.
